claim: Building 4-bit patterns from game bytes at run time costs too much per pass; make them once, keep them in spare pages and send with OTIR, and treat the cache miss cost rather than the hit rate as what sets pace.

evidence.text: Run-time building cost 113 T a byte at 28 MHz; made once and kept in spare pages then OTIR, pace came out within 0.07%.
Per-update pattern uploads of about 20k T overran the 33-66k T delay; an image-keyed cache came before limiter tuning.
Knight conversion cache misses were the cost (+2.67% from image conversions).
